plan: Define a module-level initial-session template dict so begin/abandon reset by copying one canonical state.
Store a defensive copy of appointments (id/label only, input order preserved) plus a set of known ids for O(1) validation.
Route handle(action) through a type-to-handler dispatch table, with isinstance guards so malformed or unhashable payloads yield error screens instead of exceptions.
Give each handler a validate-then-mutate structure: a shared open-session guard (active and not completed), field-specific type/membership checks, and only then a session write.

Centralize screen construction in a factory that emits exactly {prompt, messages, choices} and includes appointment choices if and only if the prompt is 'Choose appointment'; a companion error factory prefixes messages with 'Error:'.
Resolve post-correction prompts with a next-unmet-step function (contact -> appointment -> review).
Implement run_once() to raise RuntimeError before touching either port when one is missing, then read one action, handle it, display the screen once, and return that same object.
Keep I/O as injected duck-typed ports (read_action/display) so unittest fakes replace them with no non-stdlib dependencies.
mechanisms: Dispatch table mapping action type strings to bound handler methods
Validate-before-mutate guard clauses ensuring rejected actions never alter session state
Canonical initial-session template copied for construction, begin, and abandon
Screen factory enforcing the exact prompt/messages/choices shape and the choices-only-on-'Choose appointment' rule
Error-screen factory producing 'Error:'-prefixed first messages with empty choices
Dependency-injected action_source/screen_sink ports with a RuntimeError precondition in run_once()
Type-checking before hash-based membership tests to keep invalid payloads exception-free
